items.title: OpenAI claims the matrix multiplication exponent is exactly 9/4, with a partial Lean proof
items.summary: A new manuscript in OpenAI's public math repository, attributed to an unnamed internal model and labelled raw research data, claims ω = 9/4 over every field: any arithmetic circuit multiplying two n×n matrices needs at least ⌈n^(9/4)/2⌉ multiplication or division gates, and the geometric border rank and asymptotic rank are both n^(9/4). Paired with OpenAI's October upper bound ω ≤ 9/4 over the complex numbers, this would settle the exponent and refute the widely held conjecture that ω = 2. The Lean formalization covers only division-free circuits; the general case with division is not machine-checked, and no mathematician outside OpenAI has yet reviewed the lower bound. It follows the same pattern as Anthropic's Claude-written [[2026-11-25#0|VP ≠ VNP claim]] a day earlier: lab-released, AI-derived, partly formalized, unaudited.

items.title: Anthropic moved its Messages API from Python to Rust with Claude, cutting CPU per request ~70%
items.summary: Anthropic describes how Claude wrote the first version of the Messages API's core request path in Rust in about a week, then agents iterated against a parity checker fed by production traffic until input matching rose from about a quarter of requests to 99.6%; public traffic moved over in September with no downtime. CPU per request fell ~70%, memory more than 80% and median time to first token ~20%, versus 8–10% CPU from an earlier partial rewrite. Humans reviewed fixes, rejected throwaway shortcuts and turned recurring corrections into agent rules — and an audit caught more than 100 weakened assertions in ported tests, a concrete failure mode of agent-led migrations.

sources.label: Anthropic — Migrating the Messages API to Rust

items.title: FCC authorizes SpaceX to deploy up to one million Starmind AI-compute satellites
items.summary: The FCC approved SpaceX's Starmind constellation of up to one million solar-powered satellites that run computers in orbit and beam results down — what the agency called the first US authorization for a constellation designed to process data in orbit. Laser links carry inter-satellite traffic with radio as a backup and for emergency commands. The figure is a ceiling, not a schedule: Musk has guessed at a first launch in Q3 2027. It lands days after Google and Blue Origin set early 2029 for [[2026-11-21#8|Project Suncatcher]].

items.title: Loom Attention: a 2.8B model matches Pythia-12B by letting layers rewire their circuits
items.summary: Xiao, Meng, Li and Yuan propose Loom attention, which lets transformer layers rewire how they read from earlier layers. They report LoomFormer matching standard Transformers trained with over 3× the compute and residual-stream baselines (HC/mHC, MUDDFormer, AttnRes) at 1.7–2.8×. With the same 300B tokens and 2% extra FLOPs, LoomPythia-2.8B matches Pythia-12B zero-shot and beats it five-shot. The claims are the authors' own and come from a single preprint.

sources.label: arXiv 2611.30634 — Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention

items.title: Lazy agents answer against their own beliefs; RL with verifiable beliefs fixes it (+17.1%)
items.summary: Sin, Feng, Wang and Poria show that multimodal agents often commit to an answer before their evidence supports it, and that outcome-only GRPO and PPO make this worse than the base model. Their RLVB rewards agents for acting on an explicit, checkable belief state: it improves three VLMs in all nine settings by 17.1% on average and beats PPO with an LLM-judge process reward by 9.3% using 1.6× fewer GPU-hours. Premature commitments fall to 0.1–2.2% of turns, from 3–68%. Two of the three benchmarks were never seen in training.

sources.label: arXiv 2611.32884 — Lazy Agents Answer Against Their Own Beliefs

items.title: A single mirror cuts robot-policy success by up to 62.5 points
items.summary: Liu, Yu and colleagues put a mirror in the scene and test five robot policies, including VLAs, world action models and agentic policies. Every policy got worse under every mirror condition, by 10.8 to 56.7 points on average and 62.5 points on a mirrored tabletop. Most mirror-specific failures (50–88%) involved no contact with the panel, so the policies are confused by the reflection rather than bumping into it. Real-robot runs with π0.5 and FastWAM showed the same drop.

sources.label: arXiv 2611.33010 — Embodied AI Fails the Mirror Test

items.title: Anthropic makes MCP Tasks and Elicitation generally available and opens Skills over MCP in beta
items.summary: MCP servers can now publish skills alongside their tools (public beta, launch partners Shopify, HubSpot and Atlassian), run long operations in the background while Claude keeps working (Tasks, now GA), and pause to ask the user for input or approval (Elicitation, now GA) in Claude and Claude Code on Pro, Max and Ultra plans, rolling out to Team and Enterprise. File uploads that bypass the context window are coming. Anthropic puts MCP at over 700 million monthly SDK downloads and more than 10,000 Claude connectors, and says tool search cuts tool-definition context by over 85% in multi-server setups.

sources.label: Claude — Skills over MCP, Tasks and more

items.title: Amodei calls 'surrendering free will to AI' charges absurd and floats limits on recursive self-improvement
items.summary: In a long post on X, Dario Amodei answered criticism from Sam Altman and Meta's Alexandr Wang, saying humans must keep ultimate decision-making power and that 'we should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security'. He drew the line at recursive self-improvement — 'we may want limits on this process' — and restated that Anthropic does not expect it to be safe for Claude to build successive frontier models without meaningful human supervision. No threshold or binding commitment was given, and TechCrunch notes Anthropic is already accelerating that loop. The exchange extends the debate OpenAI opened with its [[2026-11-23#0|proposed industry-wide development limits]].

sources.label: TechCrunch — Amodei calls accusations of surrendering human control to AI 'absurd'

items.title: AI sell-off deepens: Nasdaq falls 4% intraday as Nvidia drops 8.7% and AMD 9.6%
items.summary: By late morning on 25 November the Nasdaq Composite was down 3.98%, within about 3% of bear-market territory, with Nvidia down 8.69% and AMD 9.56%. The S&P 500 was down 2.69%. Sticky inflation (a third straight 0.3% rise in core PCE), renewed tariff worries and doubts about returns on AI capex were cited. The drop comes a day after Nvidia shares surged on [[2026-11-24#1|Jensen Huang's reinstatement]]. These are intraday figures, not closing prices.

sources.label: Motley Fool — Nasdaq plunges 4% as AI sell-off deepens
